newsitem.title: USA: AOL Web service to use cybercash.
newsitem.headline: AOL Web service to use cybercash.

text.p: America Online Inc.'s Web hosting service, PrimeHost, will incorporate CyberCash Inc.'s technology for credit card authorisation and processing, beginning in 1997, the giant online service said Tuesday.

PrimeHost, which manages and hosts World Wide Web sites for corporations, will offer its customers secure transactions as well as software that enables customers and merchants to verify each others' identities with VeriSign Inc.'s Digital ID.
The service will cost $100 a month for unlimited transactions.
America Online, the world's No. 1 online service with 7 million members, said the new electronic commerce, or e-commerce, service will let merchants take full advantage of the Internet.
AOL said that with CyberCash's technology, secure credit card authorisations will only take seconds, from the shopper's decision to make a purchase to notification of credit approval.
Reston, Va.-based CyberCash is connected to more than 95 percent of U.S. banks and credit card processors, allowing merchants to have their choice of bank accounts.

PrimeHost was established last July and formerly was known as NaviSoft. It currently has over 2,500 customers using PrimeHost and many test users of PrimeHost's Storefront Solution electronic commerce product.

The Storefront Solution offers "store builder" software, security and verification, unlimited credit card transaction processing and Verisign Digital ID for $300 to set up and $100 a month thereafter.
America Online stock rose 75 cents to $32.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
